content.comment_body: Hello, when I attempt to transfer my program from my PC to [product_name], I can't see my Realtek PCIe GBE Family Controller in the interface. Although I can access the address of [product_name], the adapter doesn't show up so the transfer isn't possible. I tried another PC and updated JAVA, but that didn't help. I've also attached the relevant file. Assistance would be appreciated. Thank you.
Which [product_name] do you have exactly? Does the article number end with 08--[article_no]?
[product_name] software doesn't detect any Ethernet network adapter.
Where can I find that information?
I suspect there may have been an installation problem. Are there any special characters in the name of your network adapter?
It's the same situation for me.

My [product_name] (12/24RCE) article number is: 1P[article_no]-1MD08-08BA. Normally, you should see 'Realtek PCIe GBE Family Controller' on the right side. I'm using [product_name] version [version_no].

A [product_name] with the article number [article_no]-1MD08-08BA does not exist. Did you mean [article_no]-1MD08-0BA1? If so, that model requires [product_name] V8.3, which you already have. My screenshot above is also from [product_name] V8.3.
Yes, apologies, it's 0BA1 for the [product_name]. I also have version V8.3, but it doesn't detect my Intel or Realtek adapters.

When you click the down arrow, are there no options to select? If so, that's what I meant by an installation issue. What operating system are you using? If you have Windows, did you run the setup as administrator?
That's correct—there are no options displayed and I'm using Windows 10 Pro. I tried logging in as administrator as well.
That's not exactly what I meant. Did you start the installation of [product_name] software with administrative rights? You need to right-click on the installer and select 'Run as administrator'.
I tried that, but the same issue persists.
Unfortunately, I don't have a solution for your problem. You may need to start a Support Request.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering connectivity problems when using [product_name] software with Ethernet, as Realtek and Intel network adapters do not show up in the interface. Even after confirming the hardware and software versions, the adapter list remains empty and prevents program transfer. This highlights a reliability issue with the software's adapter detection, resulting in user frustration and workflow interruptions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] software to reliably recognize and display all available network adapters for easy program transfer between PC and [product_name] via Ethernet.
